issues.issue: Did the Crown's agents commit a fault in refusing his October 2010 open work permit application?
issues.applicant_position: He met the IRPR section 208 requirements, so refusing him the open work permit without cause was a fault.
issues.respondent_position: No fault: he did not meet the regulatory requirements; a work permit is a privilege, not a vested right.
issues.result_quote: CIC’s agents did not commit any fault in refusing to issue one to him.

issues.issue: Did Mr. Cissé prove damage caused by the alleged fault?
issues.applicant_position: The refusal caused him damage, including considerable mental distress.
issues.respondent_position: Damage cannot be attributed to the defendant, and no evidence of any damage was presented.
issues.result_quote: Mr. Cissé did not present any evidence relating to the damage he allegedly suffered.

issues.issue: Can Mr. Cissé raise Charter and Quebec or Ontario human rights arguments in this action?
issues.applicant_position: Raised arguments under the Canadian Charter, Quebec's Charter and Ontario's Human Rights Code.
issues.respondent_position: Objected that the required procedure for raising those arguments was not followed.
issues.result_quote: Having taken this objection under advisement, I allow it for the reasons raised by the defendant.
